about: Owner, Oct 27: every statistic starts realistic, not real, unless it is in law. Each published base-rate table (deaths, births, moves, chronic conditions, time use) is the center; each world scales the whole table once by its own factor, drawn from its seed at Start (seeded generation of the starting world). The rate still checks totals and never picks one actor's outcome (no dice).

floorShare.citation: The smallest share of the spread a world's factor takes, so no world opens on the published table.

mortality.citation: How far a world's death rates sit from the SSA 2023 period life table, as a share: about the year-to-year change in U.S. age-adjusted death rates outside the pandemic years (CDC NCHS Data Brief 521, 2010-2019 changes of 0.5% to 3%) plus the gap between period and cohort tables.
mortality.estimatedFrom: The published table is the center; a world's factor is drawn once from its seed.

spread.citation: SSA 2023 period life table; CDC NCHS age-adjusted death rates.

natality.citation: How far a world's age-specific birth rates sit from the CDC natality tables, as a share: about two years of change in U.S. age-specific fertility (NVSS Births: Final Data 2023 and 2024, rates moved 1% to 4% a year).
natality.estimatedFrom: The published table is the center; a world's factor is drawn once from its seed.

movers.citation: How far a world's leaving rates sit from the ACS 2024 mover rates, as a share: about the ACS one-year margin on state out-mover rates plus a year's change (ACS B07001, state margins 3% to 10%).
movers.estimatedFrom: The published table is the center; a world's factor is drawn once from its seed.

conditions.citation: How far a world's chronic-condition prevalence sits from the published pack, as a share: about the survey margin on adult chronic-condition prevalence (CDC BRFSS and NHIS state estimates differ from the national figure by 5% to 15%).
conditions.estimatedFrom: The published prevalence table is the center; a world's factor is drawn once from its seed.

spread.citation: CDC BRFSS state-level prevalence ranges; the condition pack's own sources.

timeUse.citation: How far a world's daily hours of unmodeled activities sit from the ATUS diary figures, as a share: about the ATUS year-to-year change in hours of personal care, household work and meals (BLS American Time Use Survey 2022 to 2024, 1% to 5%).
timeUse.estimatedFrom: The published hours are the center; a world's factor is drawn once from its seed.
